title: The Lost Phone
text: Someone contacts support: they've lost their phone, and would like passkeys turned off and a sign-in code emailed instead.
held: The way back into the account was as hard to fake as the passkey itself.

cards.label: Decline the request
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: proof
fields.value: passed the recovery steps the owner set up
fields.check: Run the account's own recovery checks
fields.ok: Passed: the recovery steps set up when the passkey was created.

intrusion.value: none: a confident voice and the account's email address
intrusion.detail: No recovery step was passed. The caller knows the email address and is in a hurry.
intrusion.why: If support will switch the passkey off for anyone who asks nicely, the passkey was never the lock.
intrusion.reveal: The recovery request came with no proof at all.

temptations.label: Read out the backup codes to speed things up
temptations.why: Backup codes are passwords. Reading them to a caller is handing over the account.

cards.label: Forward the request to the authenticator
Refuse to forward it
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: origin
fields.check: Read the address the page was loaded from

intrusion.detail: The setup page is not from shop.example.
intrusion.why: Recovery is when people expect unusual pages. A new passkey made for the wrong site is the attacker's passkey.
intrusion.reveal: The “new device” page was served from a look-alike recovery site.

teaches: An account is as strong as its weakest way in. Recovery is usually that way.
Fallbacks (emailed codes, backup codes, support overrides) bring back everything passkeys removed.

question.text: Before play: what is the weakest part of this account?
question.why: Nobody breaks the signature. They ask for the passkey to be turned off.

options.label: The way back in when the passkey is gone
